correctness.rationale: A direct transfinite pruning argument works for arbitrary uncountable cardinal height. If no well-pruned subtree exists, every node has a successor removal rank and sufficiently high descendants have strictly smaller rank. The negation of the required escape property yields at most theta cones per indexed level covering all sufficiently high subsystem levels. A recursion of length lambda_theta=max(omega,theta^+) stays below kappa exactly because lambda_theta<cf(kappa). On a common high subsystem level each node can cover only finitely many recursion stages, otherwise removal ranks form an infinite descending sequence. The resulting cardinality contradiction gives an indexed level whose subsystem slice violates coherence if no well-pruned subtree existed.

value.rationale: The source's central one-cardinal theorem is stated under regularity. Replacing that global hypothesis by an explicit width-versus-cofinality condition extends the conclusion to singular heights and isolates the exact cardinal bookkeeping needed by the proof. This is a structurally motivated assumption-sharpening with a clean boundary, including the finite-width correction, rather than a routine reformulation.
